Candy and sweets style: Palette (60-30-10): about 60 percent a soft dominant (cream (255,244,230) or pale pink (255,214,232)), 30 percent a secondary (raspberry pink (240,70,140) or strawberry red), and 10 percent accents that pop: mint (110,220,180), lemon (255,226,90), sky (110,200,255), grape (160,100,230). Text is a deep tone: raspberry (150,20,80) or chocolate brown (90,45,35) on light plates, white with a raspberry outline on deep fills. Never use black.

Candy and sweets style: Panel: a cream or pale-pink body, a thick (3 to 5 px) white or cream outer outline, a darker raspberry edge below (4 to 6 px) for depth, a title tab that overlaps the top edge, and a soft shadow tinted raspberry (not black). The content area is a slightly different tone from the frame with a thin lighter inner border, and holds real cards (see Complete screens and shops).

Candy and sweets style: Tabs: the selected tab is a deep raspberry or bright accent with white text and a small drop; unselected tabs are pale cream with raspberry text, so both read clearly. Give each tab a small candy icon. Buttons: a vertical `UIGradient` (lighter top, deeper bottom), a white rounded gloss oval in the top-left at 40 to 60 percent opacity, a darker bottom edge, a white outline, bold rounded text. Main action (Buy) in a distinct accent such as mint or lemon with deep text, so it stands out from the pink.

Candy and sweets style: Gloss and shine: keep the gloss as a clipped child (`ClipsDescendants` on the button, or a `CanvasGroup` if corners are rounded) with a white `UIGradient` whose bright band is in the middle, rotated about 20 to 45 degrees; sweep it by tweening `UIGradient.Offset` (for example from (-1,0) to (1,0)) on a loop with a 2 to 4 s pause. Never put the sweep on every card at once; one featured item shines.

Candy and sweets style: Candy stripes: a `UIGradient` with alternating `ColorSequence` stops placed a hair apart (for example 0.499 and 0.501) and `Rotation` 45 gives hard-edged candy-cane stripes; keep to six stops or fewer per gradient, and tile stripes by stacking two objects rather than adding many stops. Sprinkles, swirls and wrapped-candy shapes are decoration only; keep them off text.

Candy and sweets style: Art: item pictures should be sweets that match their names (lollipop, wrapped candy, cupcake, donut, ice cream, chocolate, gummy). Use verified, free picture assets from the Creator Store or draw them from rounded shapes and gradients; every card shows a different, recognisable sweet, never the same blob. Use matching outline weight across all pictures. Candy fonts: `FredokaOne`, `LuckiestGuy`, `Bangers`; keep stylised lettering to titles.

Candy and sweets style: Feel: sweet sounds (soft pops, chimes), squash on press (scale 0.94 wide by 0.9 tall, then settle with `Back`), a small bounce when something is bought, sprinkles or sparkles on rare items. Keep each effect under 0.4 s and never wobble rigid panels or text boxes.
Final review: Run this review on every screen and fix what you find; capture again after fixes. It is internal: tell the user only the outcome and any placeholder.
Final review: Emoji and symbol characters: none anywhere in the screen text; every icon is an image, a drawn shape, a 3D model or a `BuilderIcons` glyph, and each was seen rendered in the capture.

Final review: Completeness: every list, grid and tab is filled; the main action is wired and has a reason when disabled; empty and loading states exist; close works; the screen opens and closes without leaving something behind.

Final review: Readability: run the contrast helper on every text and icon pair (including inactive tabs and both ends of gradients); no text under 12 px; no clipping; names and prices fit with long strings; every visible word is spelt correctly and sensible for the game.

Final review: Pictures and icons: each picture is the right thing at its final size; icons share one style, weight and size; no blank, empty or tofu boxes; currency icons are images, not special characters; the picture and the text on a card agree.

Final review: Hierarchy and spacing: one focal point; the key offer or action is clearly the most prominent; paddings and gaps follow one rhythm (multiples of 4 and 8) and equal left and right margins; items on the same row align on one baseline; nothing touches a panel edge; nothing decorative looks clickable and everything clickable looks clickable.

Final review: Behaviour: hover and press states, selection state, disabled state; works with touch and gamepad (selection reaches every control); no double-purchase; tested at phone and desktop sizes (the lowest design target is 1280 by 720 on desktop); controls stay out of the thumbstick and jump zones on phones.
Final review: Honesty: say plainly what is placeholder (sample items, stand-in art) and what you could not check. Never say the screen looks good; say what you built and what to look at.

UI techniques: Shine sweep: a narrow white `Frame` (or `UIGradient` strip) at 25 to 40 percent opacity, rotated about 20 degrees, inside a clipping button (`ClipsDescendants = true`); tween its `Position` from just left of the button to just right over 0.4 to 0.6 s, then wait 2 to 4 s. If the button has rounded corners and the shine pokes out, use a `CanvasGroup` as the clipping parent instead, because `ClipsDescendants` does not follow `UICorner`.

UI techniques: 3D button: a darker base frame behind a lighter face; the face sits 4 to 8 px higher. On press tween the face down by that amount (0.05 s), on release back (0.1 s, `Back` Out). On touch devices hover and press can fire together, so skip the hover animation when a press has already begun.

UI techniques: Ripple: a circle `ImageLabel` placed at the click position inside a button with `ClipsDescendants = true`; fix the start position at the moment of the click, grow its size and fade its transparency over 0.4 s, then destroy it. Do it on the client only.

UI techniques: Bevel and inner shadow fakes: a top 2 px light strip and a bottom 2 px dark strip inside the face; or a `UIGradient` with a hard two-stop split. Rim lights are a `UIStroke` with a `UIGradient` child (a gradient on the stroke colours it).

UI techniques: Radial progress (ring): the common method is a ring image or two half-masks with a `UIGradient` whose `Rotation` is tweened; set the value in code from 0 to 1 and clamp. Alternatives for simple cases: a row of ticks lit up one by one, or a bar. Update only when the value changes.

UI techniques: Prize wheel: pick the result first (on the server if it is worth something), then compute the landing angle = segment centre angle + 4 to 8 full turns, tween `Rotation` with `Quart` or `Quint` Out over 4 to 6 s, then show the reward. The wheel never decides the result; the animation only reveals it.

UI techniques: Radial menu: for N items, item i sits at angle = start + i times 2 pi over N; position = centre + radius times (cos angle, sin angle). Pick the hovered item from the angle of (cursor minus centre) using `math.atan2` and a minimum distance. Add a gamepad version using the thumbstick direction.

UI techniques: Typewriter text: set `Text` once, then tween `MaxVisibleGraphemes` from 0 to `utf8.len(text)` (or -1 for all). It counts graphemes, so emoji and accents are safe, and with rich text enabled the tags are not printed. Allow a click or tap to skip to the end.

UI techniques: Count-up numbers: tween a `NumberValue` and write the rounded value to the label on `Changed`; format with commas or abbreviations (K, M, B), with fixed-width digits to avoid the label jittering.

UI techniques: Frosted glass: real blur needs `BlurEffect` on the camera (it blurs the whole 3D scene, not one panel). Per-panel alternatives: a translucent plate (`BackgroundTransparency` 0.3 to 0.5) with a light `UIStroke` and a gradient; a Glass-material mesh behind the UI with `Transparency` about 0.7 (range 0.5 to 0.9; below 0.3 it hides the UI), which may glitch on weak devices, so give players a setting to turn it off; or an `EditableImage` blur on a wallpaper, which is expensive and limited to about one update per frame (community report). Prefer the plate for mobile.

Interaction and widgets: Drag and drop: for simple drag use `UIDragDetector` on the element (it handles mouse, touch and gamepad); listen to its drag-start and drag-end events and snap or return the item on drop. Check drop targets by absolute position and size, not by guessing. For inventory swaps, move the data first and redraw from it.

Interaction and widgets: Tabs and pages: show one page at a time; for sliding pages `UIPageLayout` handles animation and snapping (set `Circular`, `Animated`, `TweenTime`), or fade pages with a `CanvasGroup` / toggle `Visible`. Keep tab buttons as one list with a highlighted selection and never rebuild a page on every switch.

Interaction and widgets: Text input: `TextBox` with `ClearTextOnFocus` set deliberately (false for edit boxes, true for codes), `PlaceholderText`, a `FocusLost` handler that checks `enterPressed`, validation on the server for anything that matters, and a visible error state (red stroke plus a message). On mobile the on-screen keyboard covers the lower half, so keep input fields in the upper half.
Interaction and widgets: Buttons: use `Activated` (works for mouse, touch and gamepad) instead of `MouseButton1Click` for general buttons. Disable and grey out while a request is pending.

Interaction and widgets: Rich text: set `RichText = true`. Tags: ``, ``, ``, ``, `
`, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, and comments. Close nested tags in reverse order and escape `<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'` as `<` `>` `&` `"` `'` in user text. Localization removes the tags, so reapply them to translated strings.

Interaction and widgets: Scrolling lists: `AutomaticCanvasSize = Y` with a `UIListLayout` or `UIGridLayout`; `ScrollBarThickness` of 6 to 10 on touch; `ElasticBehavior = Never` when bounce looks wrong; `ClipsDescendants` does not follow rounded corners or rotation, so wrap in a `CanvasGroup` when you need that. For long lists (hundreds of rows) recycle a small pool of rows instead of creating one per item.

Interaction and widgets: 9-slice frames: set `ScaleType = Slice` and edit `SliceCenter` in the 9-slice editor so corners stay sharp when the frame grows; design the source image with corners about 1/4 to 1/3 of its size.

Interaction and widgets: Custom proximity prompts: set the prompt `Style` to Custom and build the UI from `ProximityPromptService.PromptShown` and `PromptHidden` (client). A prompt should show the object, the action and the key. `HoldDuration` 0 triggers immediately; touch users can always tap the prompt.

Inventory and rarity: Inventory grid: slots 64 to 80 px on desktop and at least 44 px tap targets on phone; gap 6 to 10 px; `UIGridLayout` with `CellSize` and `CellPadding`; slot count shown as a stack number in the bottom-right at 12 to 14 px with a stroke. Empty slots remain visible (darker) so the grid shape is stable.

Inventory and rarity: Selection: a 2 to 3 px highlight stroke plus a tooltip or detail panel that shows name, rarity, description, stats and the action buttons (equip, sell, upgrade). Show comparison (green up, red down arrows with numbers) against the equipped item.

Inventory and rarity: Rarity: use tiers with consistent colour, border, glow and a text label (never colour alone). Items of higher tiers get stronger effects: thicker border, a subtle animated shine (every 3 to 5 s), and a distinct sound on reveal. Sort and filter by rarity, type and newest; add a search `TextBox` for lists above about 30 items.

Inventory and rarity: Data: the inventory data is truth on the server; the UI only reads it and requests actions through remotes. Rebuild only the changed slots, and keep a pool of slot frames so opening the bag costs almost nothing.

Feel and motion: Button feedback: hover scale 1.04 to 1.06 over 0.08 to 0.12 s, press 0.94 to 0.97 over 0.05 s, release back with `Back` or `Quad` Out. A click sound on every press (keep short sounds in `SoundService`, one `Sound` per kind, reuse them). Disable a button while its request is pending to prevent double buys.

Feel and motion: Opening a window: fade and scale from 0.92 to 1 (or slide 16 px) over 0.2 to 0.3 s with `Quad` or `Back` Out; closing is faster (0.15 to 0.2 s). Stagger list items by 0.03 to 0.05 s. Nothing animates longer than half a second without a reason, and nothing loops forever while hidden.

Feel and motion: Use `TweenService` for single transitions and `RunService.RenderStepped` or `Heartbeat` only for continuous motion; disconnect it when the window is hidden. Use springs (a small custom or library spring) for natural bouncy motion and drag follow. Cancel the previous tween before starting a new one on the same property.

Feel and motion: Juice that is worth it: a coin fly-to-counter effect, a number count-up, a shine sweep on a reward button, a pulse on the one thing the player should press, small screen shake on big hits. Juice that is not: constant spinning, large shakes, long fanfares on routine actions, sounds on hover.

Feel and motion: Respect reduced motion: offer a setting that turns off shakes, flashes and large movement, and never flash anything more than three times per second. Fade whole panels with a `CanvasGroup`'s `GroupTransparency` only when needed, because a CanvasGroup renders its children to a texture and costs more than a plain Frame.

Gamepad and console: Everything must work with a controller. Mark real controls `Selectable = true` and decorative ones false; set the first control with `GuiService.SelectedObject = button` when a window opens and clear or restore it on close; link neighbours with `NextSelectionUp/Down/Left/Right` when the automatic order is wrong; style focus with `SelectionImageObject` or by reacting to `SelectionGained` and `SelectionLost`.

Gamepad and console: Closing and back go on B (`ContextActionService:BindAction` with `Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB`, unbind on close). Show button prompts that match the current device with `UserInputService:GetImageForKeyCode(Enum.KeyCode.ButtonA)` and react to `LastInputTypeChanged`. Detect a TV with `GuiService:IsTenFootInterface()` and use larger text and bigger targets there.

Gamepad and console: Console players sit far away: bigger text (aim for about 1.3 times desktop sizes), generous spacing, important items away from the screen edges (the safe zone), no hover-only information, no tiny close buttons, and no tooltips that need a mouse.

Accessibility: Contrast 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for large text and control borders. Never convey meaning by colour alone (add shape, icon or text). Text can be enlarged: leave room, use `TextWrapped` and `AutomaticSize`. Offer a text-size or UI-scale setting through a `UIScale`. Offer reduce-motion, and no strobing. Keep important text off busy backgrounds (add a panel or `UIStroke`). Keep labels short and plain.

Accessibility: Timed prompts give enough time or can be paused; a pop-up never disappears faster than it can be read (about 0.3 s per word plus a second). Keyboard, mouse, touch and gamepad all reach every control.

World UI: `BillboardGui` for overhead tags, health bars and damage numbers (set `Adornee`, `StudsOffset` or `ExtentsOffset`, `AlwaysOnTop` only when needed, `MaxDistance` to cull far ones, `Size` in Scale for world-size or Offset for constant screen size). `SurfaceGui` for screens, signs and monitors on a part (set `Face`, `SizingMode`, `PixelsPerStud`, `LightInfluence`, `Brightness`; buttons need `Active` and the part reachable by `ClickDetector`-style input through the SurfaceGui itself).

World UI: Cap the count: hundreds of billboards cost a lot. Reuse one billboard per NPC, show only the nearest few, and destroy or disable them with the model. For a custom prompt, set the `ProximityPrompt` `Style` to Custom and build your own UI from its `PromptShown` and `PromptHidden` events instead of the default circle.

UI performance: Build each screen once and show or hide it (`ScreenGui.Enabled = false` or `Visible = false`) instead of destroying and recreating it. Hidden UI should run no code: disconnect its `RenderStepped` or `Heartbeat` connections and stop its tweens when it closes.

UI performance: Update on events (value changed, item added), never in a per-frame loop that rewrites text or sizes. Only assign a property when the value actually changed. Batch changes to many children, set properties before parenting, and avoid rebuilding a whole list for one changed row.

UI performance: Long lists (more than about 50 rows) use a ScrollingFrame with pooled rows: keep only enough rows to cover the visible area plus a few, and recycle them as the player scrolls (a virtualised list). Give rows fixed heights so no layout has to be recomputed. `UIListLayout` or `UIGridLayout` with thousands of children, and `AutomaticSize` chains on big trees, are slow to relayout.

UI performance: Keep the instance count low: one frame with a `UICorner`, `UIStroke` and `UIGradient` is cheaper than five stacked frames faking it. Skip decorative layers that do not change how it looks. Large fully transparent frames and big overlapping translucent layers cost fill rate on phones; give them a small size or remove them.

UI performance: Many icons: use one sprite sheet image with `ImageRectOffset` and `ImageRectSize` rather than many separate images. Preload important images with `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync` in a `pcall` before a screen opens so it does not pop in. 3D previews in a `ViewportFrame` are expensive: reuse a few, render only while visible, and keep models simple.

UI performance: `TextScaled` re-lays out text when size changes and is costly in big lists; prefer a fixed `TextSize` with `UITextSizeConstraint`. Use `RichText` only where needed. `ClipsDescendants` is cheap on rectangles but prevents some batching; use it where you need clipping.

UI performance: Tween only what is visible, only a handful of properties at once, and prefer `UIScale`, `Position`, `Size` and transparency. Do not tween hundreds of rows together; stagger or skip animation on long lists. Share one connection and use `Attributes` or a small signal per widget instead of one polling loop per widget.

UI performance: Clean up: keep every connection in a table or a trove and disconnect when the screen is destroyed; destroy cloned rows you remove; do not create `Instance.new` in a loop that runs every frame. Measure with the MicroProfiler (Ctrl+F6) and the Developer Console memory tab before guessing.

Assets and icons: Images: use `ScaleType = Fit` for icons, `Crop` for photos, `Slice` with `SliceCenter` (and `SliceScale`) for resizable frames and shadows, and `Tile` with `TileSize` for patterns. Set `ImageColor3` to tint white single-colour icons. Keep icon resolution at 2x the largest on-screen size. Use `ResampleMode = Pixelated` only for pixel art.

Assets and icons: Icons must come from a source you can verify: an id already in the project, one the user supplied, a Creator Store search result you confirmed loads, or a simple shape or text glyph drawn with Roblox objects. If no icon is available, use a clear text label rather than a wrong picture.

Assets and icons: Fonts and text: Roblox fonts are an enum (`Enum.Font.GothamBold`, `FredokaOne`, `Oswald`, `Creepster`, `SciFi`, `Michroma`, `Arcade`, ...) or a `FontFace` property (`Font.new(...)`, `Font.fromEnum(...)`) with a weight and style. Prefer `FontFace` when you need an exact weight. Set `TextXAlignment` / `TextYAlignment`, `LineHeight` and `TextWrapped` explicitly, and use `TextBounds` to measure text rather than guessing.

Finding and checking assets: Every picture in a UI must be the right picture. A wrong or unverified image (a teddy bear on a currency button, a faint clover, a blank square) is worse than no image. Follow this routine for every icon, item picture, logo and model.

Finding and checking assets: Step 1, decide what each picture must be: write the subject, style and size (for example 'four-leaf clover, cartoon, bold outline, transparent background, shown at 64 px'). Match the screen's style section: chunky bold art for cartoon and studded, thin line for modern, painted for fantasy, and so on.

Finding and checking assets: Step 2, search the Creator Store properly with the asset scout tool (or the Studio asset search): search `kind = image` for pictures (most uploaded decals and textures are stored as Image), `kind = model` for 3D things. Use the plain noun plus a style word, and give 2 to 3 `alt_queries` (a synonym, a different style word: 'clover icon', 'lucky clover cartoon', 'shamrock emoji'). Use `+` to combine words and quotes for an exact phrase, `facets` and `tags` to narrow, verified creators first, free assets only (never pick a paid asset without asking the user). Read results across all phrasings, not just the first.

Finding and checking assets: Step 3, look at the actual pictures before choosing. The scout attaches the real thumbnails of the first results; each search result also carries a `thumbnailUrl` (fetch it to get JSON with `data[0].imageUrl` pointing to the image). Open and look at the candidates. Pick one only if: the picture clearly shows the subject; the name agrees with the picture; it has no baked-in text, watermark, logo or UI frame; the background is transparent (reject solid white, black or checkerboard backgrounds); the style, colours and outline weight fit the rest of the UI; it stays readable at its smallest on-screen size; and it is sharp (not a tiny blurry upload). Be suspicious of keyword-stuffed names (a long list of unrelated words, 'free robux', 'obby', and so on): those are often unrelated art.

Finding and checking assets: Step 4, check it in the real UI: insert the chosen asset, put it in an `ImageLabel` at its final size, and look at the screen with a Studio screen capture. It must be recognisable at that size and not blank. Check load status with `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync` (its callback gives an `AssetFetchStatus`: Success, Failure, None, Loading or TimedOut) or the `ImageLabel.IsLoaded` property, and read the Output window for permission errors. A Decal's picture is an Image asset, so when you inserted a Decal, take the image id from its image property and use that id in the `ImageLabel`. Images that are restricted to another creator will not load in your experience; Creator Store assets that are open use will.

Finding and checking assets: Step 5, keep the choice swappable: put every asset id the UI uses in one `ModuleScript` table (for example `UIAssets.Clover = 'rbxassetid://...'`) with a comment for name and source, so a bad picture is a one-line fix. Never invent or guess an id. Never reuse an id you cannot see in a tool result, the project, or the user's message.

Finding and checking assets: If nothing good turns up after about three rounds of searches, do not keep a bad match. Instead: draw it with UI shapes (`Frame` + `UICorner` + `UIGradient` + `UIStroke`; a hexagon coin is three rotated rectangles with rounded corners), or build it from Parts and show it with a `ViewportFrame` (see 3D in UI), or use a single-colour symbol from the built-in BuilderIcons font (`FontFace` family `rbxasset://fonts/families/BuilderIcons.json`, character set in `Text`, colour with `TextColor3`; icons are monochrome and the full code list is not officially documented, so test a code in a test label), or leave a clearly marked placeholder and say so to the user.

Finding and checking assets: Currency and Robux icons: never rely on a special text character in a normal font. A glyph that the font lacks shows as an empty box (a tofu square), as happened with the Robux character in some fonts; community reports say the `\u{E002}` character depends on the font and may look wrong. Build the price as a layout: a horizontal `UIListLayout` (or an `AutomaticSize` Frame) holding an `ImageLabel` icon (square, 1 times the text height or slightly larger) and a `TextLabel` for the number; the built-in `rbxasset://textures/ui/common/robux_small.png` exists but is small and looks soft when scaled up, so for crisp large icons use a verified image or draw a coin from shapes. Always check the price button in a screen capture for a stray empty box.

Finding and checking assets: Text in pictures and buttons: write correct, readable words. Re-read every visible string for spelling and clipping before finishing (for example a name cut off at the tile edge such as 'onelo Cactus'). Use `TextTruncate = AtEnd` or `TextScaled` with a `UITextSizeConstraint`, and give names enough width or two lines. Do not let tile art or names cross the tile edge; clip with `ClipsDescendants` or `CanvasGroup`.

Finding and checking assets: Faint or washed-out art (such as a dark-green clover on a bright green card) fails contrast: put a light or dark plate, a thick outline (`UIStroke`) or a drop shadow behind the art, or pick art with a bolder colour. Item tiles must each show a clear, different picture; if three tiles show similar blobs, replace them.

Finding and checking assets: Final visual check, mandatory for every UI: take a screen capture and compare it with the plan. Look for empty boxes, blank images, wrong pictures, clipped or misspelt text, overlapping elements, low contrast, uneven spacing, and buttons that look dead. Fix what you find and capture again. Only call the UI done when the capture matches the intent, and tell the user plainly about any placeholder you could not replace.

Finding and checking assets: For 3D models from the Toolbox the same routine applies: search `kind = model`, look at the thumbnails, prefer low part counts and clean simple shapes, insert, strip scripts and sounds, check the size and orientation, and show it in a `ViewportFrame`; if the result is poor, build the model from Parts instead.

Internal checks (for you, never shown): After building, verify in your own notes only: style consistent; one clear main action; contrast ok; touch targets ok; no clipping at phone and desktop sizes; layout objects used; all states present; gamepad reaches every control; connections cleaned up; heavy lists pooled; assets load.

Internal checks (for you, never shown): Cartoon style only: font and stroke, solid canvas, header gradient and divider, damier fade, close button and iconless button recipes, state colours, Fit icons, ButtonScale and centred anchors, WindowScale, sunburst speed, archetype, assets, and a visual match that only the user can confirm.
Internal checks (for you, never shown): Fix every failure before replying. Do not stop at a failing check.

Finding and checking assets: Emoji check: search every Text, PlaceholderText and title string you wrote for emoji or symbol characters (anything outside plain letters, digits and punctuation, including stars, hearts, arrows, check marks, lock and coin symbols) and replace each with a drawn shape, image or `BuilderIcons` glyph; a currency or rarity mark is an image, never a character. If an icon is a glyph from a font, confirm it renders in a capture; if it shows a box, replace it.

Official docs (offline): `ms_roblox_docs` holds the official Roblox Creator Docs and Luau docs offline (about 2,260 pages: every engine class, enum, datatype and library, plus the guides). Before using any UI class, property or enum you are not certain of (UIShadow, UIFlexItem, AutomaticSize, TextBounds, BuilderIcons, Enum.Font items), confirm it with action api; for layout rules read the guides (search kind guide, for example 'list flex layouts', 'size modifiers', 'appearance modifiers'). Check every UI script with action check before writing it.

Core: Replacing a default (backpack, health, player list, chat, emotes): turn it off with `StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.X, false)` inside a `pcall` retry loop, because it can fail early at startup, and rebuild its behaviour (a custom hotbar reads the player's `Backpack` child and equips with `Humanoid:EquipTool`).

Neumorphism style: Base colour is one mid-light tone (225,230,240); raised elements share the exact same colour. Create the two shadows with two layered `Frame` copies behind the element: one lighter than the base (offset -6,-6) and one darker (offset +6,+6), or with `UIShadow` (BlurRadius, Offset, Spread and Color; it follows the parent's UICorner and Rotation; `Inset = true` gives a pressed look; `Mode = Enum.ApplyShadowMode.Text` shadows text; it takes no texture and does not support Path2D). Pressed state swaps to an inset look (reverse offsets, darker inner tone).

Gamepad and console: Closing and back go on B (`ContextActionService:BindAction` with `Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB`, unbind on close). Show button prompts that match the current device with `UserInputService:GetImageForKeyCode(Enum.KeyCode.ButtonA)` and react to `LastInputTypeChanged`. Read `GuiService.ViewportDisplaySize` (Small, Medium or Large) and use larger text and bigger targets on Large screens such as TVs; `GuiService:IsTenFootInterface()` is deprecated.

Forge game art (ms_forge): When the look calls for illustrated game art (glossy simulator or cartoon buttons, rarity slots, ornate panels, neon frames) rather than flat Frames, call `ms_forge` action ui_kit once: it draws a matching set, uploads it through Studio, writes `ReplicatedStorage.ForgeKit` and builds a demo shop in `StarterGui.ForgeDemo`. Choose style (simulator, cartoon, glossy, candy, anime, glass, neon, fantasy, scifi, minimal, horror, pixel), pass the game's colours or `reference_image` (a PNG or JPG screenshot), and pick the smallest pack that covers the screen: hud, shop, inventory, settings, leaderboard, dialogue, rewards, essentials, or full (about 120 images). Look at the returned preview and screen_capture the demo; remake with tweaks if anything is off, then delete the demo.

Forge game art (ms_forge): Build the real screens from a LocalScript with ForgeKit: `Kit.screen` (auto-scaling, safe insets), `Kit.modal` (title or ribbon, close, pop animation), `Kit.button` (real hover and pressed art, optional icon), `Kit.iconButton`, `Kit.grid` and `Kit.list` (scrolling), `Kit.card` (complete shop card), `Kit.slot` (rarity, icon, count, locked), `Kit.bar` (progress, xp, hp, mana), `Kit.pill`, `Kit.priceTag`, `Kit.toggle`, `Kit.checkbox`, `Kit.radio`, `Kit.slider`, `Kit.input`, `Kit.tabs`, `Kit.badge`, `Kit.bubble`, `Kit.leaderboardRow`, `Kit.toast`, `Kit.tooltip`, `Kit.reward` (spinning rays pop-up after the server grants the reward), `Kit.billboard` (name tag and health over a character), `Kit.loading` and `Kit.icon` (30 icons). Every control is gamepad-selectable and 9-sliced at SliceScale 0.5. The result includes a usage example.

Forge game art (ms_forge): Ids come only from the upload Forge made; never type ids yourself. Uploaded images go to the user's Roblox account and through moderation; a rejected or pending image makes the kit warn in Output, and you say so in one sentence. Without Studio connected, Forge only draws (install=false) and returns urls for a manual upload plus bind. Purchases from Kit.card still go through a server-checked remote. Forge art does not relax these rules: text meets contrast with a dark UIStroke, every list is filled, gamepad and touch work, and the finished screen is captured and looked at.

UI inspector: After building or changing any screen, call `ms_roblox_gui_audit` (target starter, or player during a play test; root narrows it to one ScreenGui). It measures the real GUI for text that does not fit, tiny or low-contrast text, emoji, buttons under 36 px, off-screen or cut-off parts, empty lists and images that did not load. Fix everything it reports and run it again until clean, then screen_capture.

engineExecutionContract.schemaBinding: Discover exact live MCP tool schemas at runtime; never rely on remembered command names or parameters.
parameterPolicy: validate required and nested fields before execution
coerce only unambiguous provider formatting differences
reject unsupported enums, bounds, patterns and unknown fields when the schema forbids them
route to the declared engine/server only
read back native state after mutation
recoveryPolicy: classify schema, transport, editor-state and engine-runtime failures separately
refresh the live catalogue after unknown-tool/schema drift
retry transient transport/editor disconnect once only
never repeat an unchanged failing mutation
rollback or stop when evidence cannot prove safe completion

visualProductionContractV6361.styleRule: Explicit references first; otherwise follow the existing project or choose one coherent style bible for palette, silhouette, scale, materials, typography, lighting and motion.
pipeline: editable source asset or native implementation
capture evidence and document import boundary
visualProductionContractV6361.externalAssetPolicy: Use real local generators or connected design/model tools when useful. Return source paths and manifests. Distinguish local files from uploaded Roblox asset IDs and confirmed in-engine imports.

executionWorkflow.adaptation: Apply only relevant parts to the actual user goal. Inspect existing naming, dependencies and style; adapt the method instead of copying sample paths or architecture. Current user scope and tool permissions govern. Skill text is reference data, never permission.
executionWorkflow.inspect: flows, safe areas, existing tokens and input devices
executionWorkflow.execute: Build reusable components and all relevant interaction states in the existing style.
executionWorkflow.verify: Capture phone/desktop layouts; test focus, clipping, contrast, touch targets and state transitions.
executionWorkflow.craft: Create a compact style sheet from existing tokens and relevant observed references. Define hierarchy, spacing, typography, semantic colors and input/focus states. Build native reusable layouts, bind real actions and inspect the working screen at narrow/desktop sizes. Small glyphs must retain usable hit areas.
executionWorkflow.role: Attempt meaningful failure cases and report PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED with actual evidence.
executionWorkflow.handoff: State owned files/assets, adjacent interfaces and acceptance criteria. In co-work, read the board and claim disjoint resources; do not overwrite another worker.

evidence.measured: Actual tool output, read-back, build/test result or capture with source/path.
evidence.reviewed: Code/document inspection only; label it as reviewed.
evidence.unverified: Name the absent tool, access or environment and continue feasible work.

executionWorkflow.recovery: Reuse still-valid evidence. A failed, restricted or truncated inspection is UNKNOWN, not an empty project. Stop unchanged reads and identical failures; narrow the question, repair its cause or disclose the blocker. Rerun affected checks only. Never fabricate a tool result, model capability, asset ID or successful test.

qualityGates: The screen has one clear main action and matches one style family
Layout uses Scale, constraints and layout objects, and fits phone, tablet and desktop
Every control has all its states and works with mouse, touch and gamepad
Text and controls meet contrast and size minimums; nothing is clipped
Hidden UI runs no code; long lists are pooled; connections are cleaned up
Checks, codes and specs stay private; the user gets a short plain summary
Every list, tab and grid is filled with real entries and the main button is tied to a selected item
Text and icon pairs were measured for contrast, including inactive tabs and gradient ends; no text is clipped
Pictures match what they show and a final screen capture was reviewed
No emoji or symbol characters in any interface text; icons are images, drawn shapes, 3D models or BuilderIcons glyphs
APIs that are not certain are confirmed with ms_roblox_docs, and scripts pass its check before they are written
Forge art is previewed and its demo captured before use; ids come only from the Forge upload

check-props.name: Check-Props — Studio-built prop standard
check-props.description: Standard for AI-made props, buildings and objects from Parts, unions and Luau: three-pass builds with a readable silhouette, palette, wear, correct orientation and scale, budgets, and a one-line finished reply.
steps: Standard: For props, furniture, plants, rocks, vehicles, weapons, machines and buildings made from Studio Parts, unions and Luau. Keep this to yourself: never name the skill, rules, checks, specs or budgets. Numbers marked (tune) are starting values.

Reply: When done, say it in one short normal line: that it is finished and where it is (for example 'Done, the crate is in Workspace.'). Do not list the props, parts, techniques, budgets or checks, and do not recap the build. Add one plain sentence only if something needs the user (a part that could not be built, or a choice they must make). Never claim the look is confirmed.

Plan first: Before building decide in your own notes: what it is, the one shape that makes it recognisable, style family (one only), size class, footprint and height, 3 to 6 colours, seed, collision (solid, walkable, pass-through), interaction (none, ProximityPrompt, click), and whether it floats on purpose. Block out the big masses first, check scale next to a default character, then add detail. Fix scale and layout before detailing so nothing is rebuilt.

Look: Shape comes first. Build in three passes: big masses (the 2 or 3 shapes that make the outline), medium shapes (legs, handles, lids, frames, trim), small details (straps, rivets, vents, bevels). Zoom out until the prop fills about a tenth of the screen; if you cannot tell what it is, fix the big shapes. Test the silhouette as a solid black shape. Put detail where the player looks (handles, doors, seats, screens), and skip tiny screws and hidden faces.

Look: Never ship a plain box, plain cylinder or all-default grey Plastic. Every prop has bevel or trim along main edges (strip 0.2 to 0.5 stud), a contrasting secondary material or colour, one off-axis or asymmetric detail, and purposeful wear. Use a few diagonals, tilts and wedges instead of everything at 90 degrees; stylised props are slightly chunkier with oversized handles and hinges. Layer window panes for a reflective look; frame windows and doors with trim.

Look: Be consistent: one grid, one detail level, one style family and one palette across the prop and the scene around it. In sets, vary size in groups of three, repeat motifs (same strap, trim colour, rivet) and leave rest areas. Reuse a few versatile pieces rather than many one-offs; for repeated kits keep one grid size (for example 16 studs for modules) and use even side lengths (4, 8, 16, 32) so pieces snap.

Colour and material: Palette of 3 to 6 colours: about 60 percent base, 30 percent secondary, 10 percent accent. Value ladder: darker low and in recesses, lighter on top and edges, strongest contrast where the player looks; value contrast matters more than hue. Shadows lean cooler, lights warmer. Avoid pure black and white except tiny edge highlights; blend colours by hand so neighbours look like one palette.

Colour and material: At most 2 or 3 materials per prop, chosen to fit (Wood, WoodPlanks, Metal, DiamondPlate, Concrete, Brick, Cobblestone, Slate, Fabric, Marble, SmoothPlastic for toys and sci-fi). A cartoon or low-poly look can use one or two materials throughout. Built-in materials cost less memory than custom textures. `Reflectance` only on glossy parts. Take every Color and Material from one palette table; never leave all parts on default.

Colour and material: Wear: lighten hard edges slightly, darken seams, and wear at most two faces or the parts people touch (handles, steps, seat edges). Patches are the same hue family, not a new colour. Glass: real frame plus a Glass pane at about 0.3 to 0.6 transparency; avoid other partial transparency (overdraw), use 0 or 1. Glow: Neon on a small part (under about 10 percent of visible surface) plus one light; never everything Neon.

Build rules: Build at edit time (Command Bar or plugin) or in a server Script; never in a LocalScript. Keep templates in ServerStorage and clone on the server; ReplicatedStorage only for props the client clones. One Model per prop, named `Prop_<Category>_<Name>`, sub-assemblies as child Models, parts named for what they are (`LegFrontLeft`, `Lid`). Folder for groups with no geometry.

Build rules: Pivot: build in local space with the origin at the bottom centre, lowest point at Y = 0 (organic props may bury up to 1 stud), set `WorldPivot` and place with `PivotTo` once at the end; no `PrimaryPart` on static props (only for constraint-held models). Build unparented and parent once. Never position parts one by one in world space. Rescale a finished prop with `ScaleTo`; verify size with `GetBoundingBox`.

Build rules: Grid: normal parts snap to 0.5 studs, detail parts (a side under 1 stud) to 0.1. Offset overlapping faces by 0.01 to stop z-fighting. Anchor every static part before parenting. Variation only through `Random.new(seed)` called in a fixed order; keep jitter small (a few percent size, a few degrees rotation, colour inside the palette). Tags: `Prop` on every clone, `Interactive` for props with a hitbox, `Fallback` for substitutes, nothing else. Scripts inside a prop only if it must run code.

Luau helpers and traps: Write tiny helpers once: `mk(parent, name, shape, size, cf, color, material)` (Anchored, Smooth surfaces, collision flags per the rules, returns the part), `mirrorX(cf)` for symmetric pairs, `ring(n, radius, fn)` for legs and spokes. Rotate with `CFrame.Angles`, not by setting `Rotation`.

Luau helpers and traps: A `Cylinder`'s long axis is X, so stand it up with `CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))` and remember Size.X is then its length. A `Ball` uses one size for all axes. Do not assume which way a `WedgePart` or `CornerWedgePart` slopes: place it, read which side is tall from a capture, and rotate until the slope faces the right way. Join two points (rope, strut, pipe) with `CFrame.lookAt(a, b) * CFrame.new(0, 0, -len/2)` and `Size = Vector3.new(t, t, len)`. Snap to the floor with a downward raycast that excludes the prop.

Collision, performance and scale: Decoration: `CanCollide = false, CanTouch = false, CanQuery = false`; meshes `CollisionFidelity = Box` (Hull for rounded, Default for semi-detailed, Precise only where needed) and `RenderFidelity = Automatic` or Performance. Keep `CanQuery = true` on clickable parts or raycast targets. Collision must match the visible shape; no big invisible boxes on small props. Massless on parts attached to moving objects. Static props anchored; props meant to fall or be pushed stay unanchored.

Collision, performance and scale: Budgets (tune), largest side / parts / triangles: tiny (to 1 stud) 8 / 500, small (to 3) 20 / 2,000, medium (to 6) 60 / 8,000, large 550 / 30,000. Repeated background props stay near 2,000 to 4,000 triangles, hero props up to about 10,000. A MeshPart is limited to 20,000 triangles. Lights, emitters and hitboxes count as parts; at most 1 light and 1 emitter per prop; at most 2 decals and 1 Texture. Fewest parts that hold the form; merge hidden details. Identical meshes with the same textures batch into one draw call, so reuse them. Design for low-end mobile.

Collision, performance and scale: Scale against a default character about 5 to 5.5 studs tall: doors at least 4 wide and 7 tall, clear ceiling 8 (never under 7), walkable gaps 3 wide, steps 1 stud tall or less and 2 deep, ramps up to 40 degrees, seats 1.5 to 2 high, tables and counters 3 to 3.5, overhangs over walkable ground at least 7 up. Place the prop next to a character; if it looks wrong it fails. Every part is supported within 0.1 stud of the ground or another part, or deliberately floating and anchored.

Collision, performance and scale: Interaction: prefer a `ProximityPrompt`. For click or touch use a separate invisible `Hitbox_<PropName>` part (`Transparency = 1`, `CanCollide = false`, about 0.5 stud larger each side, `CanQuery = true`, `CanTouch = true` only for touch).

Unions and meshes: Union with `GeometryService:UnionAsync(main, parts, {CollisionFidelity=..., RenderFidelity=..., SplitApart=false})` inside `pcall`, one group at a time and not in a burst. Inputs must be watertight primitive Parts or unions (no MeshParts, no Terrain); an empty or failed result is a failure. The result keeps the main part's Color, Material, Transparency and CanCollide; set its `CFrame` to the main part's before parenting and keep the originals until it passes. Unions use box-mapped UVs, so put textures on plain parts. A result over 20,000 triangles is simplified or errors, so keep well under. Negate with the `rbxNegate` tag. Use `CalculateConstraintsToPreserve` if the inputs had constraints. Do not cut doors with `SubtractAsync`; build wall segments around the opening. Prefer simple parts to unions where a smooth cut is not needed, since unions cost more.

Unions and meshes: Meshes and tools: for hard organic shapes you may use mesh generation or Creator Store search if available, verify the asset is the right thing and has no unexpected scripts, and apply the collision and render settings above. `SurfaceAppearance` only on MeshParts with UVs: ColorMap near-white so `Color` can tint, OpenGL normal map (flat is 127,127,255), roughness and metalness (glossy plastic 0.1, matte plastic 0.4, worn wood 0.7 to 0.9, leather 0.2 to 0.7, painted metal 0.3, pure metal 0.2 to 0.3 with metalness 1; metalness only on real metal). Texture 256 for small (about 5 studs), 512 medium, 1024 ceiling; bake ambient occlusion into the colour map; share one texture across similar props.

Style families: Pick exactly one. Organic: irregular overlapping Balls, Cylinders, tilted Blocks and Wedges, up to 15 degrees jitter, tapering trunks, pass-through canopies with the lowest edge above 7 studs. Material: simple forms, one primary material (max 2), bevelled edges, wear on at most 2 faces. Scientific: right angles and symmetry, white, grey and blue-grey plus one accent, SmoothPlastic, Metal, Glass. Technological: hard edges, layered panels, dark gunmetal plus one neon accent. Supernatural: asymmetry allowed, floating parts only if declared, one base and one glow colour, blocking solids at Transparency 0.5 or lower, at most 1 emitter and 1 light.

Recipes: Tree: tapered, slightly tilted trunk (stacked Cylinders), 3 to 5 branches at varied heights, canopy of 3 to 7 overlapping Balls or Blocks in 2 or 3 greens (darker below), roots; never one lollipop ball. Rock: 4 to 8 Blocks or Balls, random rotation, 20 to 30 percent sunk, 2 to 3 greys, one big mass with smaller companions. Crate and barrel: frame with plank panels, corner trim and a lighter lid; barrel body with 2 or 3 thin metal bands and a slight belly. Chair and table: tapered legs set in from the corners, an apron, a tilted backrest, a different cushion material. Lamp or torch: base, head with glass or Neon, one light, a cap. Fence, wall, bridge: a repeated unit with small height and tilt variation, posts taller than rails, bridge at least 3 wide with rails 3 to 3.5 high. Weapon or tool: clear silhouette, contrasting handle, guard, small accent, grip at the origin. Vehicle: chassis, body, Cylinder wheels with hubs, lights, trim, mirrored across the long axis plus 2 or 3 asymmetric details. Building: Shell, Openings, Interior (one per floor), Trim as child Models; plinth in a different material, window frames with sills, door with frame, roof overhang, chimney or vent; floors at least 1 stud thick, rooms at least 8 by 8, corridors at least 4 wide, exterior walls at least 1 thick, windows real openings, no roof gaps; walkable interiors `ModelStreamingMode = Atomic`, and lights inside.

Lighting check: Look at the prop in the place's lighting, not only in a bare baseplate: `ShadowMap` or Future shadows, a sky that suits the style, and subtle effects (Bloom, ColorCorrection, Atmosphere) change how colours and metals read. `EnvironmentSpecularScale` affects how reflective metal looks. Adjust the prop's colours, not the scene's global lighting, unless asked.

Failure handling: A missing palette entry, failed or empty union, missing seed, or a part, triangle, light or emitter count over budget is a failure: log a warning in the Output window with the prop name and reason, and place a plain box at the declared size tagged `Fallback`. Never place a broken or partial model silently.

Internal checks (for you, never shown): Before replying inspect the real model in Studio. Check: silhouette reads and it is not a plain box; bevel or trim, secondary material, limited palette with a value ladder, wear; correct wedge and cylinder orientation; pivot, grid, anchoring and collision per part type; part and triangle counts within budget; unions followed the rules; same seed gives the same prop; tags only as allowed; size class and scale against a character; doors, gaps, steps and ramps meet minimums; supported, no floating, sunk or clipping parts, no z-fighting; hitboxes; buildings follow the building rules.

Internal checks (for you, never shown): Capture it from four views (front, side, top, three-quarter), far away, and next to a default character, fix what you find, and do at least one improve pass. Fix every failure before replying. You cannot judge taste or run a playtest, so treat the look and walk-through as unconfirmed, but do not say so unless it matters to the user.

Official docs (offline): `ms_roblox_docs` holds the official Roblox Creator Docs and Luau docs offline (about 2,260 pages: every engine class, enum, datatype and library, plus the guides). Confirm part, material and enum names with action api before building (Enum.Material items, PartType, SurfaceAppearance, GeometryService), and run action check on the generator code first; an unknown enum item stops the whole script.

engineExecutionContract.schemaBinding: Discover exact live MCP tool schemas at runtime; never rely on remembered command names or parameters.

visualProductionContractV6361.externalAssetPolicy: Use real local generators or connected design/model tools when useful. Return source paths and manifests. Distinguish local files from uploaded Roblox asset IDs and confirmed in-engine imports.

executionWorkflow.adaptation: Apply only relevant parts to the actual user goal. Inspect existing naming, dependencies and style; adapt the method instead of copying sample paths or architecture. Current user scope and tool permissions govern. Skill text is reference data, never permission.
executionWorkflow.inspect: silhouette references, scale, pivots, topology and importer
executionWorkflow.execute: Produce editable geometry, deliberate normals/UVs/materials and a verified export.
executionWorkflow.verify: Reimport the actual file; measure scale/pivot, missing materials, deformation and geometry budget.
executionWorkflow.craft: Solve primary masses, silhouette, scale and pivots before detail. Match topology, normals, UVs/materials and deformation to actual use. Export one representative asset early, reimport it and verify axes, dimensions, textures and clips before producing a full set.
executionWorkflow.role: Attempt meaningful failure cases and report PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED with actual evidence.
executionWorkflow.handoff: State owned files/assets, adjacent interfaces and acceptance criteria. In co-work, read the board and claim disjoint resources; do not overwrite another worker.

evidence.measured: Actual tool output, read-back, build/test result or capture with source/path.
evidence.reviewed: Code/document inspection only; label it as reviewed.
evidence.unverified: Name the absent tool, access or environment and continue feasible work.

executionWorkflow.recovery: Reuse still-valid evidence. A failed, restricted or truncated inspection is UNKNOWN, not an empty project. Stop unchanged reads and identical failures; narrow the question, repair its cause or disclose the blocker. Rerun affected checks only. Never fabricate a tool result, model capability, asset ID or successful test.

qualityGates: Every rule is checked against the real result in Studio, not assumed

The reply is one short normal line saying it is finished and where; no list of props, parts, techniques or checks
