vfx-assets.name: VFX and Assets - effects, lighting and mood
vfx-assets.description: Always use for Roblox visual effects: particles, beams, trails, mesh effects, lightning, lighting and mood, post-processing, camera feedback, sound, performance, and Toolbox or Creator Store assets.
vfx-assets.whenToUse: Always use when adding or improving visual effects, particles, beams, trails, explosions, hit effects, lighting, atmosphere, post-processing, camera shake, sound, or Toolbox and Creator Store assets in a Roblox game.
steps: Mandatory standard for Roblox visual effects: particles, beams, trails, mesh effects, lights, lighting mood, post-processing, sky, camera feedback, sound and imported assets. Built from the official Roblox docs (particle emitters, beams, trails, lighting, atmosphere, post-processing, performance, audio) and community practice (DevForum VFX threads, lightning and shake modules, PartCache). The checks are internal; the player gets a short plain summary.

Core VFX: Effects are cosmetic and run on the client. The server sends one small, rate-limited event (effect name, position or target, maybe a seed) and each client builds the effect itself. No gameplay state depends on an effect. Never tween effect parts from the server (server tweens replicate every frame).

Core VFX: Design every effect in three beats: anticipation (a short telegraph or wind-up), the main hit (the biggest, brightest moment, usually under 0.3 s), and residue (a fading tail of smoke, sparks, glow or debris). Layer 3 to 5 simple elements (flash, core, sparks, smoke, light) rather than one complicated emitter. Vary lifetime, size, speed and rotation with ranges so no two particles match.

Core VFX: Readability first: the effect must show what happened (who, where, how big) without hiding the player's character, enemies or UI. Bright additive colours on dark scenes, darker or saturated colours on bright scenes. Keep one colour story per effect (two or three hues), brightest in the middle and dimmer at the edges.

Core VFX: Build from a template: put each effect in `ReplicatedStorage` as an `Attachment` (or a small part) with its emitters, beams, lights and sounds, set to `Enabled = false` or `Rate = 0`. At runtime clone it, place it, play it, and clean it up. Never build emitters property by property in a loop at runtime; changing emitter properties while playing can hurt performance (official).

Core VFX: One-shot effects use `emitter:Emit(count)` with the emitter's `Rate` at 0, and call `Debris:AddItem(clone, longest lifetime + 0.5)` (or `task.delay` then `Destroy`). Continuous effects use `Enabled`; to stop one, set `Enabled = false`, let existing particles finish (or `Clear()` for an instant stop), then destroy it. Pool anything that spawns more than a few times a second.

Core VFX: Scale with quality: `:Emit()` does not get Roblox's automatic graphics-level thinning, so for heavy bursts scale the count by the client's graphics level (read `settings().Rendering.QualityLevel` and map it to a 0.3 to 1 factor) and cap how many effects can play at once. Test every effect at the lowest and the highest Studio quality level.

Core VFX: Never invent `rbxassetid` numbers. Textures and sounds must come from the project, from the user, from `search_asset` / the Creator Store results you confirmed load, or from Roblox's own tutorial ids you re-confirm. If a texture does not load, fall back to the default sparkle texture or a plain shape, not an empty box.

Core VFX: Check the real result: play it in Studio (Play), look at it at a distance and close, with the camera moving, at day and night lighting, and read the Output. Anything you did not see run is reported as untested.

Particles: Parent emitters to an `Attachment` for full control (rotate the attachment to aim; `EmissionDirection` only applies on a `BasePart`). `Sphere` and `Cylinder` shapes only work correctly on a BasePart, which can be tiny and invisible. Particles spawn inside a part's bounding box or from an attachment's point.

Particles: Official limits: `Rate` at most 400 per second per emitter (100 on mobile), `Lifetime` at most 20 s, `FlipbookFramerate` at most 30. Particle count is about Rate x Lifetime. Keep Rate low and get the look from size, colour, transparency and lifetime sequences. Wide areas (rain, snow, ambient dust) use several emitters on a grid, each covering a small area.

Particles: Visual control in order of impact: Texture, Color (a `ColorSequence` over the particle's life), Size (a `NumberSequence`, with an envelope for variety), Transparency (fade in and out so nothing pops), Lifetime (a range), then motion: Speed (range, negative reverses), `SpreadAngle`, `Acceleration` (gravity, wind), `Drag`, `Rotation` and `RotSpeed`, `VelocityInheritance`, `LockedToPart`, `TimeScale`. Changing `Speed` does not change particles already alive; use `Acceleration` or `Drag` for that.

Particles: `Shape` (Box, Sphere, Cylinder, Disc), `ShapeStyle` (Volume or Surface), `ShapeInOut` (Inward, Outward, InAndOut), `ShapePartial` (Sphere: hemisphere, 1 full, 0.5 dome; Disc: inner radius, 1 is rim only; Cylinder: radius on the emission side). `Squash` stretches particles over life (positive thins and lengthens; use for rain streaks, sparks). `Orientation` is `FacingCamera` (default), `FacingCameraWorldUp`, `VelocityParallel` (streaks and sparks along motion) or `VelocityPerpendicular` (flat ground rings and shockwaves).

Particles: `LightEmission` 1 is additive and glows in the dark; 0 is normal blending. Grayscale textures with no alpha need `LightEmission = 1` to hide the dark parts. Use PNGs with a transparent background. `LightInfluence` 1 lets scene light tint the particles, 0 ignores it; `Brightness` only matters when `LightInfluence` is 0. `ZOffset` layers emitters in studs without changing size on screen.

Particles: Flipbooks: `FlipbookLayout` Grid2x2, Grid4x4, Grid8x8 or Custom with `FlipbookSizeX/Y`; leave transparent gaps between frames. Modes: Loop, OneShot (plays once over the particle's lifetime; ignores framerate), PingPong, Random. `FlipbookStartRandom` gives each particle a random start frame, `FlipbookBlendFrames` crossfades frames. Flipbooks cost extra memory and low-memory devices turn them off, so make the effect still read without animation.

Particles: `WindAffectsDrag` needs global wind (`Workspace.GlobalWind`), `Drag` above 0 and the property on. For rain, snow, ash and leaves, use `Acceleration` for fall speed (Drag slows it) and let wind push them sideways.

Particles: Roblox's own tutorial textures (confirm they load in this experience before use): spark 5833323391, smoke 5833235272, circle 6711256324, star 5860841663, swirl 5857851812, trace 5857931724, electric spark 6101261905. Two entries on that page share an id, so do not trust the heart and triangle ids.
Particles: Old `Fire`, `Smoke` and `Sparkles` objects do not accept your own textures and look dated; use `ParticleEmitter` for all of them.

Effect recipes: Explosion (a layered burst, 0.4 to 1.2 s): (1) flash: one big additive particle, Lifetime 0.1 to 0.2, Size 8 to 20 shrinking, white to orange; (2) fire core: Emit 15 to 30, Lifetime 0.3 to 0.7, orange to red to dark, LightEmission 1; (3) sparks: Emit 20 to 40, `VelocityParallel`, `Squash` 1 to 2, Speed 40 to 90, Drag 2 to 5, Acceleration down; (4) smoke: Emit 8 to 15, grey, LightEmission 0, Lifetime 1.5 to 3, grows and fades; (5) a `PointLight` that decays over 0.3 s; (6) a ring: an expanding mesh or `VelocityPerpendicular` particle; (7) a short camera shake and a boom sound. Use `Explosion` instances only with `Visible = false`, `BlastPressure = 0` and your own damage, because the built-in one kills Humanoids and breaks joints.

Effect recipes: Hit and impact (0.15 to 0.35 s): 1 to 3 flash particles, 6 to 12 sparks along the hit normal, a tiny ring, a 0.05 to 0.1 s colour flash on the target (`Highlight` fill or a brief Neon material swap), a short sound with random pitch 0.9 to 1.1. Scale everything with the hit strength. Keep it small enough for rapid repeats.

Effect recipes: Pickup and sparkle (coin, gem, reward): a burst of 6 to 14 small star particles with `LightEmission` 1, upward Acceleration, a gentle spin, a rising short chime, and a small scale pop on the item. For a collect effect, tween the item toward the player or toward the UI counter and burst at the end.

Effect recipes: Aura and charge-up: a looping emitter on the character's attachments (`LockedToPart = true`, low Rate, slow upward Speed, soft additive texture), a faint coloured `PointLight`, a pulsing `Transparency` on a mesh shell, and a rising sound; end with a flash and a burst. Disable all of it the moment the state ends.

Effect recipes: Heal, buff and level-up: rising particles and a ring expanding upward (a flat mesh scaling and fading), green or gold, a light bloom of `PointLight` for 0.5 s, a pleasant two-note sound. Show a number or icon if it matters.

Effect recipes: Magic projectile: a glowing core part (Neon), a `Trail` behind it, a small emitter at the tip, a `PointLight` with small range, and on hit an impact burst; destroy or pool the projectile. Move it on the client for visuals and let the server own the damage.

Effect recipes: Fire, smoke and embers: fire is orange-to-red with Size shrinking, `LightEmission` 1, upward Acceleration and a flickering `PointLight` (animate Brightness with small random noise); smoke is darker, bigger, slower, fading, `LightEmission` 0; embers are tiny, fast, with Drag and random drift. Put a ground glow or light on the surroundings.

Effect recipes: Dust and footsteps: a short burst of 3 to 6 soft grey-brown particles at the foot on landing or on fast steps, Lifetime 0.4 to 0.8, tinted by the floor material. Trigger it from animation markers or from `Humanoid.FloorMaterial`, and limit the rate.

Effect recipes: Rain and snow: an invisible anchored non-colliding part above the area with a high-Rate emitter facing down, positive `Squash` for rain streaks, `VelocityParallel` if streaks should follow the fall, a darker colour and higher `LightInfluence`, Lifetime tuned to end at the ground; a grid of such parts for big areas that follow the player, and tiny splash emitters on the ground. Add `Atmosphere`, a dim sky and a rain sound; use `Clouds` for stormy weather.

Effect recipes: Portal, teleport and shield: a ring or disc mesh with an animated texture or rotating Neon bands, an inward-emitting `Sphere` or `Disc` emitter with `ShapeInOut = Inward`, a coloured light, a rising hum, then a flash on the swap. A shield bubble is a slightly transparent ForceField-material or Neon sphere with a pulse on hit.

Effect recipes: Water splash and wake: an upward cone burst of round white particles with gravity, a ring on the surface, a short foam emitter, a quiet sound. Rings on water should use `VelocityPerpendicular` or a flat mesh.

Effect recipes: Muzzle flash and tracers: one 0.05 to 0.08 s flash (two crossed quads or a bright particle) at the barrel, a small `PointLight` for one or two frames, a few sparks, a `Beam` or fast `Trail` for the tracer, a shell eject particle optional. Keep it under 0.1 s so rapid fire still looks crisp.

Beams and trails: `Beam` needs two `Attachment`s (`Attachment0`, `Attachment1`) and draws a textured ribbon between them. It uses a cubic Bezier: `CurveSize0` moves a control point along Attachment0's X axis and `CurveSize1` along Attachment1's negative X axis, so rotate attachments to bend it. `Segments` sets curve smoothness (about 10 is a good start). `Width0/Width1` taper it; negative widths are reset to 0.

Beams and trails: A beam is flat, so it can vanish from the side: set `FaceCamera = true` for lasers and energy links. Use `TextureMode` Wrap or Static with `TextureLength` for repeating textures and `TextureSpeed` to scroll it; Stretch repeats `TextureLength` times across the whole beam. `LightEmission = 1` for glowing lasers. If either attachment is removed, the beam stops rendering.

Beams and trails: Layer two beams for a glowing core: a wide, soft, low-opacity one and a thin, bright, opaque one, with `ZOffset` differences of 0.01 to 0.02. Fade the ends with a `Transparency` sequence and animate by tweening Width, Transparency or CurveSize.

Beams and trails: `Trail` needs two attachments on a moving part; the distance between them is the width. `Lifetime` sets how long the trail lasts (shorter feels faster), `WidthScale` tapers it over life, `FaceCamera` keeps it visible, `Color` and `Transparency` sequences fade it. Use it for weapon swings, projectiles, dashes and vehicles. Disable the trail (`Enabled = false`) when the object stops or you teleport it, or you get a streak across the map.
Beams and trails: Beams and trails render per player quality; check them at the lowest graphics level (a beam used to imitate a curved slash loses its curvature at low quality).

Mesh effects: For slashes, shockwaves, rings, domes and energy shells use simple meshes (flat ring, squashed sphere, cone, cylinder) with a transparent texture, `Material = Neon` or a bright colour, `CanCollide = false`, `CanQuery = false`, `CanTouch = false`, `Anchored = true`, `CastShadow = false`. Animate with `TweenService`: grow Size, rotate, fade Transparency to 1, then destroy.

Mesh effects: Slash arc: a curved mesh (a slice of a squashed sphere) with a streak texture, spawned at the weapon, rotated along the swing, grown quickly over 0.1 to 0.2 s and faded. To keep the mesh itself transparent, apply the image through `Texture` objects on its faces instead of its `TextureId`; scrolling a sprite sheet by changing the texture offset gives a stronger slash. Trails and beams can imitate it cheaply.

Mesh effects: Shockwave: a flat ring (or cylinder) scaled from small to large over 0.25 to 0.5 s with `Quad` or `Exponential` Out easing and Transparency 0 to 1, plus a dust ring of particles. A dome is a half sphere scaling up and fading. Stack two at different speeds for depth.

Mesh effects: Keep meshes cheap: low triangle counts, one shared mesh and texture reused across effects (identical mesh plus texture can be instanced into one draw call), `RenderFidelity = Performance` for distant ones, no unions. Translucent parts cost more to render than solid ones, and fully transparent (1) parts are almost free; `Neon` and `ForceField` materials are more costly than `SmoothPlastic`.

Mesh effects: Do not set a part's transparency in a per-frame loop for dozens of parts; tween a handful, or use `CanvasGroup`-style tricks only in UI. Destroy or pool effect parts the moment they finish.

Lightning: A bolt is a chain of short segments between two points, with each middle point offset sideways by random noise, and often a few thinner side branches. Generate it with a seeded `Random` created once; keep segment length around 1 to 4 studs for short bolts and add layered noise for a living look. Bezier curves let it arc rather than run straight.

Lightning: Cheap rendering: use a `Beam` per segment chain (attachments moved to the points) or thin Neon parts from a pool (PartCache style); the Part-based version looks best but costs the most, and community modules cap a profile at 6 to 7 bolts for performance. Flash it (re-roll every 0.03 to 0.06 s for 0.2 to 0.4 s total), add a quick `Bloom`-friendly bright core, a light flash, a camera shake and thunder with delay by distance.

Lightning: Run it on the client from a server `RemoteEvent` (position, target, seed). Disable it when far from the player. Prefer a maintained module (such as the community Lightning Beam, EasyBolt or Lightning Module) if the project already has one; read its source and cap its settings.

Lighting and mood: Start from `Lighting.Technology` (set in the Studio Lighting properties). Future is the most realistic and most expensive; ShadowMap and Future are the costliest options; devices that cannot run Future fall back automatically. Pick by the game's art goal, not by default, and test on a phone.

Lighting and mood: Main Lighting levers: `Brightness`, `ExposureCompensation` (lower exposure needs higher Brightness and brighter local lights), `Ambient` and `OutdoorAmbient` (hue of shadows and outdoors), `ColorShift_Top` and `ColorShift_Bottom` (sun-facing and away tints), `ClockTime` (0 to 24), `GeographicLatitude`, `EnvironmentDiffuseScale` and `EnvironmentSpecularScale` (0 to 1), `GlobalShadows`, `ShadowSoftness` (0 to 1, Realistic style only), `LightingStyle` (Realistic or Soft) and `PrioritizeLightingQuality`.

Lighting and mood: Mood recipes: Horror: low Brightness (0.5 to 1), ClockTime 0 to 2, dark blue-green Ambient (10,12,18), cold or sickly ColorShift, `Atmosphere` Density 0.3 to 0.45 with Haze 2 to 2.8 and a grey-green Color, a weak flashlight `SpotLight`. Sunny: Brightness 2 to 3, warm ColorShift_Top, light `Atmosphere` Density 0.2 to 0.3, `SunRays` low. Sunset: ClockTime 17.5 to 18.2, `Atmosphere` Glare 0.6 to 1 with Haze 1.5 and a warm Decay, warm OutdoorAmbient. Night city: ClockTime 0 to 1, bright coloured Neon and `PointLight`s, `Bloom` Intensity 0.5 to 1, cooler Ambient. Treat these as starting points and tune by eye.

Lighting and mood: `Atmosphere`: `Density` (0 to about 0.35) is how much air blocks the view, `Offset` (0 to 1) blends distance into the sky (low) or makes a horizon (high), `Haze` (about 1 to 2.8) adds hue and distance haze, `Color` tints it, `Glare` adds sun glow and needs Haze above 0, `Decay` shifts hue away from the sun and needs Glare and Haze above 0. It needs a sky. Balance Offset with Density, because a low Offset can let the skybox show through terrain. `Lighting.FogStart/FogEnd/FogColor` is the simple alternative.

Lighting and mood: Local lights (`PointLight`, `SpotLight`, `SurfaceLight`): keep the count low; Future caps per-pixel and shadowed lights per frame. Shadow cost from cheapest: narrow `SpotLight` (under about 120 degrees), narrow `SurfaceLight`, then `PointLight`, which is by far the most expensive; wide spot lights cost almost as much as point lights. Turn `Shadows` off unless the shadow is the point, limit `Range` and `Angle`, and disable lights outside a range or room. Colour lights to match the effect.

Lighting and mood: Sky and weather: `Sky` takes six seamless face textures (`SkyboxBk/Dn/Ft/Lf/Rt/Up`); `SunAngularSize`, `MoonAngularSize`, `StarCount`, `CelestialBodiesShown`, and `SkyboxOrientation` (applied Y, then X, then Z; wrap the Y value with `%` when animating a slow spin). `Clouds` must be a child of `Terrain`; `Cover` 0 to 1 and `Density` low for light clouds, high for stormy ones; global wind moves them. Terrain water is set on `Terrain` (colour, reflectance, transparency, wave size and speed); a thin Foil-material slab under water adds sun reflections.

Lighting and mood: Materials: `Neon` and `Glass` need light and contrast to look right; glass refraction is not supported on mobile; `MaterialVariant`s in `MaterialService` give custom tiling materials by name; use `SurfaceAppearance` for UV-mapped meshes. Square textures work best.

Post-processing: Effects live in `Lighting` for everyone or in the player's `Camera` for one player (use the camera for a menu blur or a hit flash). `BloomEffect` (Intensity, Size, Threshold) makes bright things glow: lower Threshold and moderate Intensity make neon pop, but too much washes everything out. `ColorCorrectionEffect` (Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, `TintColor`) sets the grade and gives feedback (red tint at low health). `DepthOfFieldEffect` (FarIntensity, NearIntensity, FocusDistance, InFocusRadius) is best for cutscenes, shops and previews. `SunRaysEffect` (Intensity, Spread) gives a sun halo; objects in front shape the rays. `BlurEffect` (Size) blurs the whole 3D view (the standard way to blur the world behind a menu).

Post-processing: Use a small, consistent grade for the whole game (a slight Contrast and Saturation lift, a tint matching the mood) and tween temporary effects in and out: 0.1 to 0.3 s in, 0.3 to 1 s out. Destroy or reset them when done. Many stacked effects cost GPU time on phones; use few, and test at low quality because some effects do not show at low settings.

Post-processing: Hit flash and impact frames: a 0.05 to 0.1 s `ColorCorrection` flash or brief white/black tint, optional Neon colour swap on the hit parts (save and restore their Material and Color), then restore everything. Keep them short, rare and optional for players sensitive to flashing (never flash more than three times per second).

Camera and feedback: Camera shake: compute a small offset per frame and multiply it onto the camera CFrame (`camera.CFrame = camera.CFrame * offset`) from a `RunService:BindToRenderStep` at a priority just after the camera (`Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1`), never replace the camera CFrame. One-shot shakes for impacts and explosions (magnitude, roughness, quick fade in and out), sustained shakes for earthquakes, engines and charging. Falloff with distance from the source; keep magnitude small and offer a reduce-motion setting. A well-known module (RbxCameraShaker, EZ Camera Shake, SimpleShaker) with its presets is fine; do not rely on an unmaintained one.

Camera and feedback: FOV kicks: tween `Camera.FieldOfView` by 3 to 10 degrees for dashes, sprints and hits and back within 0.2 to 0.5 s. Combine small FOV, short shake and a sound for punch. Do not stack many at once.

Camera and feedback: Hit-stop is hard on Roblox (physics cannot be paused locally). Fake it by slowing only the attacker's and victim's animation tracks (`AnimationTrack:AdjustSpeed(0.1)`) for 0.04 to 0.08 s, then restoring, plus the flash and shake.

Camera and feedback: Damage numbers, popups and pickups: a `BillboardGui` that floats up 3 to 5 studs, fades and scales in 0.6 to 1 s, with crits larger and in a hotter colour; pool them and cap the count. Screen vignette and a red tint for low health are a `ColorCorrection` tint or a UI gradient.

Sound: Sound makes effects feel real. Add a sound to every meaningful effect: impact, whoosh, sparkle, ambience. Use short assets, random `PlaybackSpeed` 0.9 to 1.1 so repeats do not sound identical, and 2 or 3 variations for frequent sounds. 3D sounds use `RollOffMode` and `RollOffMaxDistance`; sounds in a `SoundGroup` share volume and effects such as reverb (parent the group to `SoundService`).

Sound: Check `Sound.IsLoaded` (or wait for `Loaded`) before `Play()` or reading `TimeLength`, preload important sounds with `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync` (in a `pcall`), and destroy one-shot sounds when `Ended`. Do not play dozens of the same sound in one frame: aggregate or cap. `SoundService.AmbientReverb` sets cave or room reverb on the client. Newer audio uses `AudioPlayer`, `AudioEmitter`, `AudioListener` and wires with effects like `AudioReverb`, `AudioEqualizer` and `AudioCompressor`; use them when the project already does.
Sound: Unload long music when it is no longer needed because large sounds use a lot of memory. Sounds are client-side feedback: the server only triggers the event.

Timing and sync: Sync effects to animation with markers: add named markers in the animation and connect `track:GetMarkerReachedSignal("Name")` to spawn the VFX and sound at the exact frame; clean up on `track.Ended` (not `Stopped`, which fires before a fade finishes). Verify the sync again if you change `AdjustSpeed`.

Timing and sync: Use `RunService.Heartbeat` for simulation-time effects and `BindToRenderStep` (Last priority) or `PreRender` only for visuals that must follow the camera; disconnect them when the effect ends. Use `Debris` or `task.delay` for timed cleanup, never a `while` loop that polls.

Timing and sync: Place effects relative to the right object: an effect following a moving part is parented to an `Attachment` on that part (or uses `LockedToPart`); a one-shot at a hit point is placed at the hit position facing the surface normal. Particles in the far distance may stop rendering if the emitter's attachment is not streamed in; keep ambient effects near the camera.

VFX performance: Fill rate and overdraw are the main particle costs: cost scales with Rate x Size x opacity x overlap. Reduce big, overlapping, translucent particles first (shorter Lifetime, smaller Size, fewer layers) before lowering Rate. Reuse textures (reuse costs less memory than unique ones); flipbooks and large textures use extra memory. A 1024 x 1024 texture uses four times the memory of 512 x 512; most effects need 512 or less and minor ones under 256.

VFX performance: LOD: disable ambient emitters beyond about 100 to 300 studs and halve their Rate at half that distance, using a coarse timer or zone check rather than a per-frame loop over many emitters. Spawn ambient effects only near the camera. Preload flipbooks and key textures before combat or in the loading screen.

VFX performance: Cap concurrency: a global limit on simultaneous effects, drop low-priority cosmetic ones first when over budget, and skip effects that are off screen or far away. Pool parts (PartCache-style) and emitter clones for anything fast and repeated, resetting every changed property when reusing.

VFX performance: Lights: few and small. Shadows off on small, distant or moving objects (`CastShadow = false` on small parts). Avoid layered transparency. Instanced identical mesh plus texture reduces draw calls. Check Studio's Stats (Render, GPU, draw calls via Shift+F2) and the MicroProfiler before and after.

VFX performance: `Highlight` is limited per client (a community summary puts it at 255 instances, disabled ones included), so remove or reuse them; check behaviour on a real phone if the effect matters there. Avoid high emission and many tweens at once; avoid changing emitter properties at runtime.
VFX performance: Keep `ReplicatedStorage` effect templates light; store server-only assets in `ServerStorage`. Remove effect connections and instances on character removal and player leave.

Style and polish: Pick a style and hold it: stylised (flat bright colours, chunky shapes, short bold bursts), realistic (soft gradients, smoke, subtle light), anime (sharp slashes, impact frames, speed lines), or neon/sci-fi (glow, thin lines, grids). Do not mix.

Style and polish: Timing curve: fast in, slower out. Most hits peak in 2 to 4 frames and fade over 10 to 20. Use easing (`Quad`, `Back`, `Exponential`, `Elastic` for bouncy) for size and transparency sequences, never raw linear unless it is a scroll.

Style and polish: Add secondary motion (small sparks, drifting dust, a ground ring) and a light/colour reaction on nearby surfaces. Value hierarchy: the brightest value is the focus. Silhouette: the shape should read at a glance, even small on a phone.

Style and polish: Gameplay telegraphs (incoming attacks, danger zones) are clear, consistent and visible before impact; ambient effects never mimic them. Keep sound, light and camera feedback in proportion to the action's importance.
Toolbox and Creator Store assets (official guidance): Check the creator and rating, and inspect an asset before inserting it.

Toolbox and Creator Store assets (official guidance): Some assets include scripts that run on their own. Read every script in a model before use, delete scripts you do not need, or use Disable Scripts on the object.
Toolbox and Creator Store assets (official guidance): Prefer assets with no scripts and write the behaviour yourself following code-quality.
Toolbox and Creator Store assets (official guidance): Check part count and texture sizes before adding; heavy models cause lag.
Toolbox and Creator Store assets (official guidance): Never invent an asset id. If you cannot confirm an id loads, say so and use a placeholder.
Toolbox and Creator Store assets (official guidance): Store used models in ServerStorage (server only) or ReplicatedStorage (clients need them) and clone at runtime.

Docs (look here before guessing an API; class pages are at https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/<ClassName>): ParticleEmitter, Beam, Trail, Attachment, Lighting, Atmosphere, Sky, Clouds, BloomEffect, ColorCorrectionEffect, DepthOfFieldEffect, SunRaysEffect, BlurEffect, PointLight, SpotLight, Highlight, Debris, Sound, SoundGroup, TweenService, RunService, ContentProvider, AnimationTrack, Camera, MaterialService; guides https://create.roblox.com/docs/effects/particle-emitters and https://create.roblox.com/docs/performance-optimization/improve

Audio: Two systems exist: the Audio API (`AudioPlayer` wired to `AudioEmitter` or `AudioDeviceOutput`, with effects such as `AudioReverb`, `AudioEqualizer`, `AudioCompressor` in the chain) and classic `Sound`. Follow what the project uses; do not mix both for one feature. For 3D put an `AudioEmitter` on the part; with `SoundService.AcousticSimulationEnabled` (Audio API) walls muffle sound and rooms reverb, and `BasePart.AudioCanCollide = false` stops a part blocking it.

Audio: Sounds started on the client are heard only by that client (UI clicks, music, feedback); sounds started on the server replicate to everyone, so prefer a remote telling clients to play locally, which also respects each player's volume. Preload only critical sounds with `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync`. Pool frequently played sounds. A sound in a part that streams out stops, so keep ambience in persistent models or `SoundService`. Give players separate Music and SFX volume sliders and a mute.

Audio: Audio assets must be owned by the experience owner or shared with it, or free-to-use Creator Store audio; otherwise they fail with permission errors in the Output. `AudioTextToSpeech.AutoLocalize` translates text per player; turn it off for names and chants.

Lighting and effects (engine facts): `Lighting.LightingStyle` is `Realistic` or `Soft` (stylised) and replaces the superseded `Technology`; `Atmosphere` replaces fog; animate `ClockTime` on each client from `workspace:GetServerTimeNow()` instead of replicating it. Limit shadow-casting lights; `Highlight` count is limited. `Explosion` sets off physics: for visual-only set `DestroyJointRadiusPercent = 0` and `BlastPressure = 0`. Spawn cosmetic effects on clients and destroy or pool them. `ParticleEmitter:Emit(n)` for bursts; `Beam` for lasers and ropes; `Trail` for swords and projectiles.

Talking to the player: The user wants plain input and plain output, like any player or developer: they ask for a thing, they get the thing. Never mention skills, standards, checks, rule codes, ids, budgets or internals.

Talking to the player: Reply in one to three short plain sentences: what is done and, only if needed, one thing to try or one thing you could not confirm. No lists of rules, no tables, no process notes.
Talking to the player: Do every check yourself and fix failures before replying. Never claim it works or looks good unless you ran it or measured it.

fix-errors.name: Fix Errors — Roblox error and bug triage
fix-errors.description: Always use when a Roblox game has an error, a bug, something not working, or lag: read the real Output, find the cause, make a small fix and re-run.
fix-errors.whenToUse: Always use when something is broken: an error in Output, a script that does nothing, UI or data or an NPC not working, or lag.
steps: Process: Read the actual error before touching code: the full message, the script name and the line number from Output (or the Developer Console, F9, for a live server). Reproduce it once. Do not guess.

Process: Open the script at the line named. Fix the cause, not the symptom: never hide an error with pcall, an extra nil check that skips the feature, or by deleting the feature. Keep the change small.
Process: After the fix run the same steps again, confirm the error is gone and the Output has no new errors or warnings, and check the neighbouring paths you touched. Remove any temporary prints.

Process: An error inside an event handler or task.spawn kills only that thread, so the rest of the game keeps running and the real problem can be far from the symptom. Read the first error in the Output, not the last.

Process: Decide which side the problem is on. Use the Test tab with a Server and Client window, and check Output for the server and client views separately. A LocalScript error is a client error; a Script error is a server error.

Error 'attempt to index nil with X': the thing before the dot is nil. Causes: the object does not exist yet (use WaitForChild, or on a client check streaming), wrong name or path, the character respawned, the object was destroyed, or FindFirstChild returned nil. Find which value is nil and why.

Error 'X is not a valid member of Y': wrong name or capitalisation, the child is not there yet (it has not replicated or streamed in), or it exists only on the other side (server-only objects such as ServerStorage contents never reach clients).

Error 'Infinite yield possible on WaitForChild': the child never appears. Check the exact name, the real parent, and whether the object is created on the other side. Add a timeout and handle the missing case.
Error 'attempt to call a nil value': the function does not exist. Check spelling, that the module returns it, and dot versus colon (obj:Method() passes self, obj.Method() does not).
Error 'attempt to compare number with nil' or 'perform arithmetic on nil': a value was never set. Check attribute and leaderstat names, default values, and load order (data not loaded yet).
Error 'Script timeout: exhausted allowed execution time': a loop without a yield. Add task.wait, or split the work across frames, or fix the loop condition.

Error 'Requested module was required recursively' or 'module experienced an error while loading': two modules require each other, or the module itself errors at the top level. Break the cycle by passing dependencies in or moving shared code to a third module.
Error 'Maximum event re-entrancy depth exceeded': a property or event handler changes the thing that fires it. Guard with a flag or disconnect first.
Error 'Studio access to API services is not enabled' (DataStore) or 'HttpService is not enabled': turn on the setting in Game Settings, Security, and publish the place first; Studio needs it.
Error 'DataStore request was throttled' or 'added to queue': too many requests. Reduce and batch requests and add backoff.
Error 'Failed to load sound/asset' or 'Asset is not trusted': the id is wrong, was moderated, or the experience is not allowed to use it. Say the asset needs replacing; never invent an id.
Error 'Unable to cast value to Object' or 'invalid argument #1 (number expected, got nil)': a wrong or missing argument. Print the type and value passed in.

No error but a script does nothing: a LocalScript only runs in places like StarterPlayerScripts, StarterGui, StarterCharacterScripts, the Backpack or ReplicatedFirst; a Script only runs in the Workspace or ServerScriptService (or with the right RunContext). Check Enabled/Disabled, the parent, and that it is not inside a Model that is never loaded.

No error but a remote does nothing: name mismatch, the remote is not in ReplicatedStorage, wrong direction (FireServer vs FireClient), the server handler was connected after the client fired, or the server rejected the request in its validation. Log on both sides.

No error but UI does not show: ScreenGui Enabled, Visible, size of 0, ZIndex or DisplayOrder, ResetOnSpawn clearing it, ClipsDescendants, transparency 1, or it was parented to the wrong place. Check AbsoluteSize and AbsolutePosition.
No error but data does not save: API services off in Studio, place not published, saving before the load finished, key mismatch, or BindToClose not waiting. Check Output for DataStore warnings.

No error but Touched or a prompt does not fire: CanTouch or CanCollide off, both parts anchored (Touched needs a moving physics part), ProximityPrompt not parented to a BasePart or Attachment, Enabled false, MaxActivationDistance or line of sight.
No error but an NPC does not move: anchored parts, no network ownership set, PathStatus not Success, wrong agent size, or the Humanoid is dead.
No error but an animation or sound does not play: the asset is not loaded or not permitted for this experience, the Animator is missing, or the track was not stored and was garbage collected.

Works in Studio but not live (or reverse): permissions and API services, StreamingEnabled, server versus client timing, unpublished changes, or a Team Create sync issue. Test with a real server and a second client.

Lag or stutter: use the MicroProfiler and Script Profiler to find the cost before changing anything. Common causes: per-frame loops, too many parts or particles, unbounded tables, connections that were never disconnected.
Verify: reproduce before, fix, reproduce after, and read the Output again. Report untested if you could not run it.

Output window (official): filter by type (Error, Warning), by context (Client, Server, User Plugin) and by text; Show Source adds the script name and line; Show Context tags each message as client or server; Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) clears it. Clear it, reproduce once, then read from the top.

DataStore codes (official): 403 API access not enabled in Studio; 301 to 306 request queue full (slow down and retry); 401 and 402 server shutting down (do not retry); 105 value over 4 MB; 101 and 102 empty or over-long key (max 50 characters); throttled errors retry with backoff.

A part or model is nil on a client only: streaming may not have sent it yet. For an Atomic model WaitForChild on the model itself; for Persistent models wait for Workspace.PersistentLoaded; do not expect ReplicatedStorage contents to stream; local-only changes are lost when something streams out.
A prompt does something it should not: Triggered fires on the server for any player who triggers it, even out of range, so add the distance, cooldown and state checks.

Docs (look here before guessing an API; class pages are at https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/<ClassName>): https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/output; https://create.roblox.com/docs/cloud-services/data-stores/error-codes-and-limits; https://create.roblox.com/docs/workspace/streaming; https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/ProximityPrompt; https://create.roblox.com/docs/performance-optimization/design

Common errors and causes: `X is not a valid member of Y`: the child does not exist yet or is spelt differently; use `WaitForChild` (with a timeout) on the client, check the exact name and parent, and remember server-created objects may replicate late. `attempt to index nil with 'X'`: the thing before the dot is nil; find which variable is nil and why (a failed lookup, a response with a different shape, a player who left). `attempt to call a nil value`: calling a function or method that does not exist on that value (a table has no `:Destroy()`; a misspelt method).

Common errors and causes: `attempt to iterate over a nil value`: the list is nil; check the real shape of the data (print it) and that the request succeeded, because HTTP and DataStore results are often nested one level deeper or empty after a rate limit. `attempt to compare number with nil` or `attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value`: a missing attribute, value or leaderstat. Assigning a wrong type to a property (a string to `Size`) errors; convert it. `Infinite yield possible on ...` is a warning that a `WaitForChild` is never satisfied: wrong name, wrong parent, or the object is created only on the other side.

Common errors and causes: Missing or extra `end`: count the blocks that open against the ends; the editor underline and the error line show where. A script in the wrong place does not run (server Scripts in ServerScriptService or Workspace, LocalScripts in StarterPlayerScripts, StarterGui or StarterCharacterScripts, ModuleScripts anywhere both sides can reach). `HttpService is not allowed` or HTTP 403, 429: enable HTTP requests in settings and back off on rate limits.

Remotes and networking: RemoteEvent not firing: (1) create remotes on the server and keep them where both sides can see them (ReplicatedStorage), (2) the same exact name on both sides, (3) the client uses `WaitForChild` and the server connects `OnServerEvent` before the client can fire (create the remote and connect first; for startup use a RemoteFunction handshake), (4) the server handler's first parameter is the player; do not pass LocalPlayer yourself, (5) the print after `FireServer` only proves the client ran, check the server output.

Remotes and networking: In Studio use Test with a server and clients (Server and Client windows); when a local server runs, server prints show in the server output, not the client's, which looks like the event never fired. Validate every argument on the server (type, range, ownership, cooldown). Tables sent through remotes lose metatables, non-string keys may change, and instances only arrive if they exist on the receiving side.

Debugging method: Reproduce first, then narrow. Use the debugger when a bug is not obvious: a breakpoint on the suspected line, a conditional breakpoint for a specific value (`id == 10`), a logpoint to print without editing code, and the Watch and Call Stack windows to see values and who called. Step Into F11, Step Over F10, Step Out Shift+F11. Set the breakpoint context (Client, Server, Edit) to match where the code runs.

Debugging method: Without the debugger: `print` at the start of the script, inside the branch and inside the loop to find where it stops; `warn` for non-fatal problems; `error` to stop on a missing requirement. Check the Developer Console (F9) for client and server logs, memory and network, and the MicroProfiler for slow frames. If nothing prints at all, the script is not running: check its location, whether it is disabled, its RunContext, and whether an earlier error stopped it.

Data and purchase errors: DataStore errors carry a code: 101 empty key, 102 key over 50 characters, 105 value over the size limit, 301 to 306 throttled (queue full: slow down and batch), 401 and 402 shutting down, 403 Studio API access off, 5xx server trouble (retry with a backoff). Always `pcall`, log the message, and never write default data after a failed read.

Data and purchase errors: Players charged but not rewarded almost always means two scripts set `ProcessReceipt`, the handler returned nothing for a missing player, or it errored; keep one handler, return `NotProcessedYet` when unsure and `PurchaseGranted` only after saving.

Silent failures: Animation does not play: the asset is not owned by or shared with the experience owner, the track was loaded on the wrong side, or the Animator is missing. Sound silent: audio permission error in the Output, started on the server in a part that streamed out, or wrong volume. Studio DataStore errors: API access is off. Remote works in Studio but not live: ordering at startup, or an instance the receiver cannot see (ServerStorage, not yet streamed). Scripts from free models doing odd things: check for hidden scripts. Fix the cause and re-run to confirm the Output is clean.

Talking to the player: the user wants plain input and plain output. Never mention skills, standards, checks, rule codes or internals. Reply in one to three short plain sentences: what was wrong, that it is fixed, and one thing to try. No lists, no tables.
Talking to the player: do every check yourself and fix failures first. Never say it is fixed unless you re-ran the same steps and the error is gone; if you could not run it, say so in one sentence.
qualityGates: The same steps are re-run after the fix and the error is gone
No new errors or warnings appear in Output
Errors are never hidden with pcall or by removing the feature
Anything not run in Studio is reported as untested in one plain sentence
The cause of each error was found from the message and line, not hidden with pcall
